Eggs incubated at 25 °C [T = 25 °C] typically undergo chorion rupture approximately 1.25 days [ab = approximately 1.25 days] after fertilisation, a developmental rate derived from observations on the closely related Clarias gariepinus and applied here to the hybrid Vundu (Heterobranchus longifilis x Clarias gariepinus). At a higher incubation temperature of 33 °C [T = 33 °C], this same hatching event occurs markedly faster, with eclosion recorded after only 0.58 days [ab = 0.58 days], highlighting the strong thermal sensitivity of early embryogenesis. The newly emerged yolk-sac larva has a minute mass, and volumetric calculations based on a mean egg diameter of 1.4 mm yield a wet weight at birth of approximately 0.0014 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.0014 grams]. This extraordinarily low neonatal mass, typical of teleosts that produce large numbers of small pelagic eggs, places the larva in a highly endotrophic phase where it relies entirely on its yolk reserves for several days before the onset of exogenous feeding. These early life-stage parameters underscore the hybrid's capacity for rapid hatching under warm conditions, a trait that may confer advantages in thermally variable environments.

As the yolk-sac larva transitions to an exogenously feeding juvenile, somatic growth accelerates dramatically, and field surveys of adult populations indicate that individuals can attain a maximum recorded total length of 150 cm [Li = 150 cm]. Exceptional specimens, however, have been documented at 180 cm and 45.5 kg, though the asymptotic length under typical environmental conditions appears to cap near the 150 cm mark. Concomitantly, the ultimate wet weight of a fully grown adult in natural waters is considerable, reaching up to 55 000 grams [Wwi = up to 55 000 grams]. This immense body size, characteristic of large clariid catfishes, is associated with a relatively slow life-history pace at the population level, with individuals requiring substantial time and resource accumulation to approach these maxima. The growth trajectory from a 0.0014 gram [Wwb = 0.0014 gram] hatchling to a 55 000 gram adult  represents an increase of nearly eight orders of magnitude, an ontogenetic feat that demands efficient feeding and metabolic strategies across multiple size classes.

Sexual maturation in this hybrid is attained only after a period of sustained somatic growth, and pubertal development is defined by the achievement of a minimum body mass rather than a strict chronological age. The wet weight at puberty has been estimated at 1200 grams [Wwp = 1200 grams], a value consistent with observations that individuals begin to exhibit gonadal recrudescence when they exceed approximately one kilogram. At a stable water temperature of 29.5 °C [T = 29.5 °C], the mean gonadosomatic index (GSI) was recorded at 1.3% [GSI = 1.3%]. This strategy may reflect an iteroparous reproductive mode in which females spawn repeatedly over an extended season, distributing their reproductive effort rather than concentrating it into a single massive investment.

Lifespan data for Vundu, again derived from long-term captive studies on parental species, indicate that the maximum longevity under standard conditions reaches 4380 days [am = 4380 days] when maintained at 29.5 °C [T = 29.5 °C], which positions the hybrid as a relatively long-lived teleost compared to many other large catfishes, a life-history trait that is often linked to delayed maturity and low natural adult mortality. In practice, wild individuals may experience shorter lifespans due to predation, fishing pressure, or resource limitation, yet the physiological potential for a decade or more of reproductive activity underpins the population's capacity for resilience.

Comparative analyses across the Clariidae family reveal that the hybrid's total length of 150 cm places it among the largest members of this group, although the record specimen of 180 cm demonstrates that exceptional individuals can exceed this size considerably.
